basics.name: Filipe Pinarello Scalcon, Ph.D.
basics.label: Research Associate
basics.summary: Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering with a focus on control applied to power electronics for applications in industry, electric traction and renewable energy conversion. Over 35 applied research publications, including 9 top-tier IEEE journal papers and 23 IEEE international conference proceedings (h-index 11). Over 10 years of engineering experience spanning industry and academic research at leading programs, with direct involvement in 4 industry-academia projects.

work.company: Department of Electrical and Software Engineering, University of Calgary
work.summary: Leading technical direction of the microgrid research project.
highlights: Led technical direction of the microgrid research project, coordinating efforts across electrical and chemical engineering groups
Assumed full ownership of laboratory operations, including safety protocols, equipment maintenance, and onboarding of new team members
Supervised 2 PhD and 2 MSc students, providing research guidance and performance oversight
Collaborated directly with the principal investigator to define strategic priorities and long-term research direction
Expanded publication output and contributed to grant writing and project reporting

work.company: Department of Electrical and Software Engineering, University of Calgary
work.summary: Contributed to the construction and optimization of a campus microgrid facility.
highlights: Contributed to the construction and optimization of a campus microgrid facility, incorporating solar panels, microinverters, a Chroma battery system, a propane generator, and a flow battery
Assisted in coordinating day-to-day laboratory operations, including safety compliance, personnel training, and system maintenance
Mentored and collaborated with 2 PhD and 2 MSc students on research related to electric machine control and 3-phase grid-tie systems
Supported the principal investigator in shaping the research roadmap
Authored and published research findings in peer-reviewed journals

work.company: McMaster Automotive Resource Centre, McMaster University
work.summary: Worked on three industry-sponsored projects with Enedym and Cubic Transportation Systems.
highlights: Worked in three industry sponsored projects in teams of upwards of 15 people and in close proximity of the company engineers
Explored automatic code generation for TI DSPs using Simulink and transferred functionalities from legacy C code, later validated in an experimental setup

Implemented different high performance control techniques for SRMs, such as an initial position estimation algorithm for sensorless operation, current control strategies for high speed SRMs, and techniques for RMS capacitor current reduction
Contributed to the development of an IoT edge device for machine vision and image recognition using an NVIDIA Jetson platform
Elaborated several technical reports, journal and conference papers
Assisted the ECE department in activities such as participating in the interview of candidates for faculty positions

work.summary: Proposed new methods for the advanced control of switched reluctance motors.
highlights: Proposed new methods for the advanced control of switched reluctance motors
Collaborated with external researchers from McMaster University
Published 8 high-impact journal papers during a 2.5-year period
Worked closely with a group of approximately 10 graduate students, acting as a mentor to some of them

work.summary: Initiated the research on switched reluctance and synchronous reluctance motors.
highlights: Initiated the research on switched reluctance and synchronous reluctance motors in the institution
Quoted, designed and built an experimental setup for synchronous reluctance machines
Led a project with a budget of approximately 15k USD

work.summary: Assisted graduate students with experimental setups and surveyed motor control strategies.
highlights: Assisted graduate students with the assembly of experimental setups
Surveyed control strategies for induction and permanent magnet synchronous motors
Researched the control of six-phase BLDC motors

work.summary: Full-time internship in product verification and validation.
highlights: Carried out the instrumentation of combines and planters using a plethora of sensors
Performed data acquisition and post processing analysis for engineers
Implemented a remote position control circuit for a hydraulic pump, allowing safe operation of the equipment during destructive tests
Tested parts from alternative suppliers seeking cost reduction
Awarded with continuous improvement goals achievement as a member of the PV&V department
